title: One relative compact-flat-generator extension
statement: Let $Y$ be any scheme and let $L,E$ be cochain complexes of module sheaves on $Y$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $a:L\to E$ be a chain map. Suppose $L$ and $E$ are each zero above an integer, with possibly different bounds. Suppose every term $L^i$ is isomorphic to a coproduct $\bigoplus_{j\in I_i}G_{i,j}$ indexed in the scheme universe, where the $G_{i,j}$ are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and have the following finite-support property: for any family $(H_k)_{k\in K}$ indexed in that universe, every map $G_{i,j}\to\bigoplus_{k\in K}H_k$ factors through the canonical inclusion of a finite subcoproduct. Then there exist a bounded-above complex $L\prime$, maps $l:L\to L\prime$ and $v:L\prime\to E$, with $v$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], $l\gg v=a$, and every $l^i$ a split monomorphism. Every term of $L\prime$ is likewise a universe-small coproduct of flat module sheaves with the same explicit finite-support property. No hypothesis of quasi-isomorphy, monicity, or epimorphy is imposed on $a$.

source.place: Proof, relative cone induction before the final termwise-surjectivity addition; affine-open resolving class from 03EW and 077J, as expanded in lean/Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/FlatTelescopeTargetRefinement.lean, original first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Construct the functorial compact-flat-generator cover. Take S to be coproducts of such generators, and prove every zero object is in S by an empty coproduct. The cone of a:L→E is bounded above by max(bL,bE), since its terms are L^{i+1}⊕E^i. Apply the existing cycle-pullback construction with S and this cover.

The cycle-pullback lifting property proves the augmentation Q→Cone(a) a quasi-isomorphism. Apply Mathlib mono_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements to lift a cycle mapping to a boundary one degree down, and epi_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements to lift a target cycle with zero next-degree component.

Apply the explicit relative biproduct cone extension to Q→Cone(a). It gives the bound, quasi-isomorphism v, strict equality l≫v=a, split components, and term isomorphisms Lprime^i≅L^i⊕Q^i. Reindex the two generator coproducts by the disjoint union of their index types: explicit Sigma.desc and biprod.desc maps give the isomorphism by their universal properties. Flatness and finite support follow separately on each summand, with no compactness hypothesis on Lprime itself.

proof_origin.place: Explicit cone coordinates, compact affine generators from 03EW, and existing cycle-pullback construction; no new sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_compact_flat_generator_relative_extension (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (L E : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (a : L ⟶ E)
    (hL : ∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero (L.X i))
    (hE : ∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hgen : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (I : Type u)
        (G : I → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)),
        Nonempty (L.X i ≅ ∐ G) ∧
        (∀ j : I, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (G j)) ∧
        ∀ (j : I) (K : Type u)
          (H : K → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
          (f : G j ⟶ ∐ H),
          ∃ (S : Finset K) (g : G j ⟶ ∐ (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ H k.1)),
            g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ Sigma.ι H k.1) = f) :
    ∃ (L' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
      (l : L ⟶ L') (v : L' ⟶ E),
      (∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero (L'.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso v ∧ (l ≫ v = a) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, IsSplitMono (l.f i)) ∧
    ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (I : Type u)
        (G : I → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)),
        Nonempty (L'.X i ≅ ∐ G) ∧
        (∀ j : I, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (G j)) ∧
        ∀ (j : I) (K : Type u)
          (H : K → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
          (f : G j ⟶ ∐ H),
          ∃ (S : Finset K) (g : G j ⟶ ∐ (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ H k.1)),
            g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ Sigma.ι H k.1) = f
